props.label: The Librarian's Index
props.note:
Candlekeep keeps what the realm knows. Here's where to look:

· The Wayfinder's Atlas, open on the globe table: every road and door.
· The Shopkeepers' Ledgers, on the shelves right of the north aisle: who sells what, and for how much.
· A Field Guide to the Creatures, on the shelves left of the north aisle: what lives where, and what can be hunted or tamed.
· The Almanac of Stream and Hedge, right of the south aisle: fish and foraging.
· A Short History of the Village, left of the south aisle.

If something here has gone out of date, say so. It will be corrected in the margin, never torn out.

props.label: The Wayfinder's Atlas
props.note:
Open on the globe table. Every road in the realm is written here, so nobody has to guess the next door.

FROM HOME
Home Hearth → The Crossroads (the round fire with the sofas).
From the Crossroads there are four roads:
· Hero's Journey → The Prancing Pony
· Dusty Trails → The Saloon
· Black Serenity → the Ship's Bridge
· Home, Home → back to the Hearth

THE VILLAGE
The Prancing Pony → Village Square, or back to the Crossroads.
Village Square → Candlekeep (top middle), Larkspur Goods (centre), the Wizard's Tower (top left), the Prancing Pony (left).

THE WILD COUNTRY
Wizard's Tower (Outside) → into the Tower, back to the Village, down to the Enchanted Forest, or on to the Fey Court Approach.
Enchanted Forest → Forest Depths (north, up the path), Forest Clearing (east), back to the Tower (south).
Forest Depths → the Feywilds, the Wild Edge, the Clearing.
The Feywilds → Feywilds Depths → Fey Court Approach → round again to the Tower.

The shortest way from home to the forest is Hearth, Crossroads, Pony, Village Square, Tower, Forest. That's six doors. I counted them with my own feet. — B.

props.label: A Field Guide to the Creatures of the Realm
props.note:
What lives where, what can be hunted, and who might come home with you.

THE ENCHANTED FOREST (all three glades)
To hunt: rabbit, deer, boar, wolf, and rarely a black wolf.
To tame: squirrel (by day), raven (any hour), wolf (at dusk), owl (only at night), and two rare, dangerous ones: a bear cub (mind the mother) and a venomous snake.
Victor always wants pelts and rabbits. Ask him for work.

THE FEYWILDS
To hunt: rabbit, deer.
To tame: wolf, hawk, rabbit. Flicker the bunny lives there and will show you round.

THE WILD EDGE (north of the forest)
To tame: hawk, or a bear cub if you are brave.

THE WIZARD'S TOWER
Ravens and owls keep the tower company.

THE VILLAGE
Cats, rabbits and squirrels in the square, and a cat at the Prancing Pony.
Candlekeep has its own raven. Be polite to it. It keeps accounts.

NOTICE: The alpha wolf has been seen prowling Village Square. It is very dangerous. Do not go alone.

CLOSER TO HOME: the Woods behind Home
Only gentle wild things live there, and nothing will hurt you. Wolf at dusk, cat any time, owl at night, rabbit at dawn, hawk and squirrel by day, raven any hour, hedgehog at dusk, badger at night. How you approach matters more than luck, so speak gently, bring food, and know their nature.

QUICK ANSWERS
A fishing rod: Victor sells them for 6 or 18, or you can craft one from 4 firewood and 2 thread.
A longbow: Larkspur Goods, 55.
The cheapest arrows: Victor's, at 1 each, or 5 for a single piece of firewood.

props.label: A Short History of the Village
props.note:
as far as the shelves remember

CANDLEKEEP has been here forever. Nobody remembers it being built, and the founding page has never been found. The village grew up around its doors, not the other way round.

LARKSPUR GOODS has passed down through the Larkspur family for decades, growing from a market stall into the shop on the square. Cassian keeps it now. He's been behind its counter since he was six years old.

THE PRANCING PONY belongs to Bran Morrison, who bought it with his savings and has spent his years since feeding people. Folk say he walked harder roads before he settled. He doesn't talk about them, and he knows every traveller by name.

MISTRESS ELOWEN THISTLEDOWN came out of service in the great houses and bought the modest tower near the Feywilds to study in peace. The village invited her in early on. Not everyone was easy about her magic at first, and Bran brought her bread anyway.

VICTOR THE RANGER keeps the forest. He talks more to trees than to people, and he has always protected the village from the woods. A little bunny named Flicker found her way to him and never left.

There are empty pages at the back of this book. History is still happening.

props.label: The Almanac of Stream and Hedge
props.note:
FISHING
Enchanted Forest stream: trout, perch and salmon; rarely a golden carp; once in a blue moon an enchanted koi.
Feywilds pools: pixie fish, moonfish and starlight bass; rarely a fey dragon eel or a prismatic koi.
Wild Edge river (strong currents): catfish, bass and pike; rarely a giant catfish.
Bare hands will do, barely. A rod helps, and bait helps more: worms, minnows and magic lures are all at Victor's.

FORAGING
Enchanted Forest: wildflowers, healing herbs, forest mushrooms, oak branches. Brown caps, Victor says. Not the red ones.
The Feywilds: glowing mushrooms, enchanted acorns, and rarely fey blossoms and moonpetals.
Outside the Wizard's Tower: arcane moss, and rarely a mana crystal.
Every patch needs a little rest between pickings.

description: Candlekeep is a broad stone library laid out around a circular blue-lit reading table. Four banks of tall bookcases divide the floor into quiet aisles, with smaller reading tables and chairs tucked against the outer walls. Blue runners bearing gold stars lead in from the lower entrance and continue towards an arched door at the far end. Stained-glass windows, candles and wall lamps pick out the stone pillars; spiral stairs rise in both upper corners. The shelves make the room feel enclosed and orderly, while the open central crossing leaves a clear place to pause between the stacks.
